title: Proposal: Native Current Date Rendering with the <date> Element

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

body:
### What problem are you trying to solve? HTML currently has no native mechanism for dynamically displaying the current local date or its individual components without JavaScript or server-side rendering. A common example is displaying the current year in a copyright notice: ```html
Copyright ©
``` Other use cases include displaying the current day, month, or complete date in a specific numeric format, such as DD/MM/YYYY. These are simple and common requirements, but they currently require JavaScript, server-generated content, or external libraries. A native HTML solution would make this functionality available directly in markup, simplify static websites, reduce boilerplate, and allow browsers to handle date updates automatically. ### What solutions exist today? Today, authors can display the current date using JavaScript, server-side rendering, or third-party libraries. For example, JavaScript can generate the current year: ```html ``` The existing HTML element can represent a specific date or time, but it does not automatically calculate and display the current date. Server-side rendering can generate the date before the page is delivered, but the displayed value can become outdated if the page remains open across midnight. These approaches work, but they introduce additional code or infrastructure for a relatively simple presentation requirement. There is currently no standard HTML syntax specifically designed to render the current local date and automatically keep it up to date. ### How would you solve it? I propose introducing a native HTML element with a part attribute that determines which part of the current local date is rendered. Individual components would be supported: ```html ``` The element would also support a combined numeric date format: ```html ``` For October 19, 2026, the expected output would be: ```text 19/10/2026 ``` Additional formats could include: ```html ``` When the part attribute is omitted, the element would default to YYYY-MM-DD. The proposed behavior is as follows: - The date is calculated using the user's local time zone and system date. - The day and month are rendered as unpadded numbers when requested individually. - DD and MM are zero-padded to two digits in combined formats. - YYYY represents the four-digit year for years 0000–9999. - The element updates automatically when the local calendar date changes, including across local midnight. - Changes to the part attribute trigger recalculation. - The functionality requires no JavaScript, network request, permission, or page reload. The initial implementation should use the proleptic Gregorian calendar to ensure predictable numeric output. If the part attribute contains an unsupported value, the browser should fall back to YYYY-MM-DD without breaking document parsing. I recognize that introducing a new HTML element may not be the preferred approach. An alternative would be to extend the existing element with equivalent functionality. I would welcome discussion about which approach best fits HTML's existing semantics and design principles. ### Anything else? _No response_
